attributes.external_dependencies: ["subprocess (provider CLIs: aws, az, gcloud, terraform, ldapsearch)", "urllib/ssl (product admin APIs)"]
attributes.purpose: Effects of live read-only collection: running collectors' calls (subprocess commands with credentials on stdin only; in-process HTTP GETs, and POSTs of a read-only query's JSON body to URLs the collector declares (Collector.queries, refused in connectors.collecting otherwise), with TLS trust from the record and client certificates via memfd) and resolving credential references once per run, in memory, with redaction of error output

attributes.description: importer ejbca/inventory (inventory.py: export ejbca/<source>/cas.json, certificates/<CA id>/page-<n>.json, profiles/<name>.json, count.json; completeness: pages vs total_certs, total changing, readable count > seen -> incomplete; root CA empty search -> denied), profiles.py (validity in EJBCA's notation, EKUs, available_cas), collect.py (GET /v1/ca, optional GET /v2/certificate/count, POST /v2/certificate/search per CA paged at 500 sorted by ISSUED_DATE, GET /v2/certificate/profile/{name}; Collector.queries declares the search). Least-privilege role proven live against keyfactor/ejbca-ce:9.6.3 (marker ejbca).
attributes.external_dependencies: ["EJBCA REST API v1/v2 (Community 9.6.3 tested; protocols REST Certificate Management and V2 enabled), client certificate (mutual TLS)", "opsdir-adapter-x509 (certificate_facts incl. endpoints; cryptography)", "keyfactor/ejbca-ce:9.6.3 docker image (live tests only)"]
attributes.purpose: Keyfactor EJBCA read into the core pki domain over its REST API, metadata only: CAs (named by subject CN, ciamProviderRef the EJBCA name), revocation endpoints from the latest active certificate's extensions, certificate profiles as CA-scoped templates, issued-certificate inventories with template, requester and revocation reason; a client-certificate collector whose v2 certificate search is the only (declared, read-only) POST.

attributes.name: provenance
attributes.purpose: What a call runs, in words that never hold a credential: the command line, GET and the URL, or POST, the URL and the read-only query's body (the evidence's provenance).

attributes.name: refused
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "call", "type": "Command|Request|str", "required": true}, {"name": "queries", "type": "tuple[str]", "required": false, "description": "the collector's read-only query URL patterns (Collector.queries)"}]
attributes.purpose: Why a call is never run: a step that is a problem text, a POST (Request with a body) to a URL the collector's queries don't declare a read-only query or an observing one, a debug switch on a command; else None.

attributes.name: run_call
attributes.purpose: Effect: (output, problem) of one call: a Command run as a subprocess, a Request made as an HTTP GET or the POST of its read-only query's body as JSON (an observing one's answer, whatever it is, as its output); (None, None) when it says there is nothing to read (its absent markers).

attributes.name: certificate_facts
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "pem", "type": "str", "required": true, "description": "PEM text whose first certificate is read"}]
attributes.purpose: The public facts of a PEM certificate as the record writes them, CA-neutral (any CA's issued-certificate importer): serial (lowercase even-length hex), SHA-256 fingerprint (ciamFingerprint's form), subject and issuer (RFC 4514), validity (GeneralizedTime), extended key usages (OIDs; None when the certificate has no EKU extension) and the revocation endpoints it names ((kind, url), ...: CRL distribution points crl, freshest CRL delta-crl, OCSP ocsp, CA issuers ca-issuers; URIs only), what a CA whose settings can't be read (EJBCA over REST) is known to publish; None when the text isn't a certificate. Never a key.
attributes.returns: {"type": "dict | None", "description": "{serial, sha256, subject, issuer, not_before, not_after, usages, endpoints} or None"}

attributes.name: is_query
attributes.purpose: Whether a POST Request's URL path is one of the read-only query endpoints its collector declares (regular expressions searched in the path).

attributes.name: validity_days
attributes.purpose: Whole days (rounded up) of an EJBCA certificate profile's validity in EJBCA's notation (1y 6mo 3d 12h 30m: a year 365 days, a month 30), with why not when it isn't one (an absolute end date, which isn't a length).

attributes.name: offered_to
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "profile", "type": "dict", "required": true, "description": "a GET /v2/certificate/profile/{name} answer"}, {"name": "ca", "type": "str", "required": true, "description": "the CA's EJBCA name"}]
attributes.purpose: Whether an EJBCA certificate profile answer offers the CA (its EJBCA name) to issue from: available_cas names it or ANY_CA.

attributes.name: profile_template
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true}, {"name": "ca", "type": "str", "required": true, "description": "the record's CA name"}, {"name": "ejbca_ca", "type": "str", "required": true, "description": "the CA's EJBCA name"}, {"name": "name", "type": "str", "required": true, "description": "the certificate profile's name"}, {"name": "profile", "type": "dict", "required": true}, {"name": "ee_profiles", "type": "tuple[str]", "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: (the CA-scoped template entry of an EJBCA certificate profile the CA issued from, or None, notices): cn '<CA>/<profile>', description naming the end entity profiles its certificates came through, the longest validity in days, its extended key usages; rights not read (Community REST exposes no roles, approval profiles or DN override): None. A profile no longer offered to the CA is left out, named.

attributes.name: certificate_pem
attributes.purpose: The PEM of an EJBCA search answer's base64Cert (base64 of the PEM body as EJBCA 9.6 sends it, or of the DER), or None when it holds no certificate data.

attributes.name: issued_facts
attributes.purpose: (the issued-certificate facts of one EJBCA search result, the x509 facts or None): read from its certificate (certificate_facts) when EJBCA stored it, else from EJBCA's columns (no SHA-256); the template '<CA>/<certificate profile>', the end entity username as requester, revocation date and RFC 5280 reason when revoked (status 40/60 or a revocation date).
attributes.returns: {"type": "tuple", "description": "(facts dict of ISSUED_ATTRS, x509 facts dict | None)"}

attributes.name: page_path
attributes.purpose: The export path of one CA's n-th certificate search page for a collection source: ejbca/<source>/certificates/<CA id>/page-<n>.json.

attributes.name: profile_path
attributes.purpose: The export path of a certificate profile answer for a collection source: ejbca/<source>/profiles/<name, percent-encoded>.json.

attributes.name: listed_cas
attributes.purpose: The CAs of a GET /v1/ca answer ({id, name, subject_dn, issuer_dn, external}, ...), or None when the text isn't one.

attributes.name: search_page
attributes.purpose: (certificates, total_certs or None, problem or None) of a saved v2 certificate search page: an error answer or text that isn't one is a problem.

attributes.name: profile_names
attributes.purpose: The certificate profile names the certificates of search results name, in first-seen order.

attributes.name: read_ca
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true}, {"name": "source", "type": "str", "required": true, "description": "the collection source's name (ejbca/<source>/)"}, {"name": "listed", "type": "dict", "required": true, "description": "the CA as GET /v1/ca lists it"}, {"name": "files", "type": "dict", "required": true, "description": "the export"}, {"name": "when", "type": "str", "required": true, "description": "GeneralizedTime of the inventory"}, {"name": "extra", "type": "tuple[str]", "required": false, "description": "problems every CA of the source shares (EJBCA counting more than the reader saw)"}]
attributes.purpose: (Imported groups, notices) of one EJBCA CA of a collection source: its authority (ciamProviderRef its EJBCA name) with the revocation endpoints its most recently issued active certificate other than its own names (a root's sub-CA certificates count; none: the record's kept), its issued-certificate inventory (complete; incomplete: a page missing or failed, the pages not holding the counted total, the total changing, extra; denied: a root's search empty) and its certificate profiles as CA-scoped templates.

attributes.name: read_inventory
attributes.purpose: Imported (importer ejbca/inventory): per collection source in the export and per CA it lists, the CA with its revocation endpoints, its issued-certificate inventory and its certificate profiles as its own templates, each replacing the record's; dated by --at.

attributes.name: base_of
attributes.purpose: The REST API base (https://<host>:<port>/ejbca/ejbca-rest-api) of an ejbca/inventory collection source location (https://<host>:<port>/ejbca), or None when it isn't an https URL.

attributes.name: search_body
attributes.purpose: The JSON body of the read-only v2 certificate search for one page of a CA's certificates (CA EQUAL its name, sorted by issue date, PAGE_SIZE per page).

attributes.name: kept
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "fields", "type": "tuple[str]", "required": true}, {"name": "items", "type": "dict", "required": false, "description": "{list field: its items' fields}"}]
attributes.purpose: A Request keep function: a JSON answer reduced to the fields the importer reads (top level, and per item of its list fields); text that isn't JSON kept as it is.

attributes.name: inventory_steps
attributes.purpose: Collector steps for ejbca/inventory per readable source (client-certificate): GET /v1/ca and the optional count; per CA it lists (not external) the first search page; then the rest of the pages its total names and each certificate profile the certificates name.

attributes.name: source_problems
attributes.purpose: Why ejbca/inventory collection sources can't be read: their own problems, a credential scheme other than client-certificate, a location that isn't an https URL.

attributes.definition_json: {"url": "str", "headers": "((name, value), ...) no credentials", "credential": "(basic|bearer|token|api-key|client-certificate, ref, login, ...) | (headers, ref, login, (login_header, secret_header)) | None", "ca": "ref of a PEM certificate | None", "absent": "tuple[int]", "keep": "fn(output) -> output | None", "observe": "bool: the answer, whatever it is, as an observation's JSON text (core.observation); never a failed call", "body": "str | None: a read-only query's JSON text; the Request is then a POST of it (Content-Type application/json), only to a URL its collector's queries declare, never a credential, never observing"}
attributes.description: An HTTP call a collector asks opsdir to make itself: a GET, or the POST of a read-only query's body (EJBCA's certificate search) to a URL its collector declares a query (Collector.queries, enforced by connectors.collecting.refused); an observing one (observe=True, GET only) records whatever the endpoint answers (a revocation endpoint's binary answer as base64) or why it answered nothing
attributes.name: Request

attributes.definition_json: {"importer": "str", "scope": "environment|estate", "steps": "fn(d, m, done, options) -> ((path, Command|Request), ...)", "verify": "fn(d, m) -> (call, check(output) -> problem|None) | None", "problems": "fn(d, m, options) -> (problem, ...) | None: why it can't collect here (nothing run)", "options": "tuple[CollectOption] = (): the run-time options it takes, offered as `opsdir collect` flags (U.14 task 519)", "queries": "tuple[str] = (): regular expressions searched in a URL's path: the read-only query endpoints it may POST a body to; any other POST is refused (task 561)"}
attributes.description: How opsdir collect reads one importer's export from the live system, read-only (Adapter.collectors), the options it takes (CollectOption: the CLI builds its collect flags from the installed collectors' declarations) and the read-only query endpoints it may POST to (queries).
attributes.name: Collector

attributes.description: Milestone 108 item (e), EJBCA part (deferred note 3228 on file 1119; research in decision 3210). Read EJBCA (Keyfactor; Community 9.6 / Enterprise 9.7) into the CA-neutral pki model (flow 60), metadata only. (1) Core: the collector Request is GET-only today (opsdir/opsdir/live.py, core/contract.py); add a read-only POST (a search body, no state change) under the existing collector contract, least privilege and evidence; this worker OWNS live.py/contract.py changes in this round. Reuse the 'client-certificate' credential scheme from task 558 for mTLS. (2) A new adapter package (decide name at design, e.g. opsdir-adapter-ejbca): collector (GET /v1/ca, POST v2 certificate/search paginated, GET v2 certificate/profile/{name}, v2 endentity/profiles/authorized) and a saved-export importer (pure) that parses base64Cert with opsdir-adapter-x509 certificate_facts; certificate profiles (+ end entity profile) as CA-scoped templates (ciamTemplateAuthority, cn '<CA>/<profile>'); revocation status/reason/date; CRL/OCSP/AIA defaults aren't in REST (Known limit or ConfigDump). (3) Validate live against the keyfactor/ejbca-ce container (sources disagree on whether Community has certificate search: find out). (4) Tests, showcase change, README/docs. Design gate to the master before coding if the record changes. Reserved: core attrs 900-909, classes 195-196; showcase CHG-2121, A282-A285, B112-B113.
attributes.name: EJBCA issued-certificate inventory (POST collection, mTLS)
